pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Leverage and cover are weak, and the apparent improvement is partly a perimeter effect. Total debt to trailing Adjusted EBITDA was 8.13x at FY2025, 7.75x at the trailing period to Q1 2026 and 7.16x at the trailing period to Q2 2026, but each earlier ratio uses a window with fewer Windstream months, so the improvement is partly a perimeter effect rather than a deleveraging. Cash interest cover was 1.78x, 2.34x and 1.94x on the same windows. Mechanism (Analyst Interpretation): higher-cost debt added in 2026 (8.625% unsecured notes and the asset-backed notes) is likely to raise cash interest faster than Adjusted EBITDA at the current build stage. Implication: leverage tolerance is low and a modest earnings shortfall would push trailing cash interest cover to about 1.55x (illustrative, calculated below). - Free cash flow is structurally negative while the build runs. Operating cash flow less capital expenditures was negative 459.8 million in H1 2026 and negative 437.6 million in FY2025. Adjusted EBITDA less capital expenditures for the trailing period was 151.4 million (calculated below), which does not cover trailing cash interest paid of 768.6 million. Mechanism: capital expenditures at Kinetic of 602.8 million in H1 2026 front-load cost before subscriber revenue. Implication: the company depends on debt issuance or asset monetisation to fund both the build and interest, and creditors depend on continued access to the asset-backed and bond markets. - Management's 2026 outlook implies interest absorbs most of the trend in earnings. The outlook for Adjusted EBITDA is 1,450 to 1,500 million, interest expense, net 805 million and a net loss of 480 to 530 million (management forward-looking statement). Against first-half interest expense, net of 383.9 million, the outlook implies about 421.1 million in the second half (calculated). Outlook Adjusted EBITDA covers outlook interest expense, net 1.80x to 1.86x (calculated). Implication: GAAP losses persist through 2026 on the company's own outlook. - Maturity profile is back-ended by instrument due dates but the printed table conflicts. By due date, 876.5 million falls due in 2027 and 2028 (the convertible notes and the 4.75% secured notes) and 7,405.1 million in 2031 to 2033. Within that, the 6.50% unsecured notes of 1,110.0 million fall due in 2029, and the 8.625% unsecured notes plus the 2025 Term Loan, 2,595.0 million together, fall due in 2032. The Q2 10-Q prints a maturity table that places 886.5 million in 2027 and 1,120.0 million in 2028, which differs from the due dates by one year for 2027 to 2030; the Q1 10-Q table agreed with the due dates. This corrects the financial base handoff, which said no maturity table was printed: one is printed at Q2 10-Q page:30. The credit view uses the due dates and flags the conflict. Implication: the wall by year is uncertain by one year for 2027 to 2030 until the company confirms the schedule; the total is not in question. - Structural priority is shifting toward asset-level debt. Of total principal, 6,964.1 million is secured (credit facility and secured notes 5,165.0 million plus asset-backed notes 1,799.1 million) and 3,716.5 million is senior unsecured, including the 2027 convertible notes (calculated; the convertible notes are described as senior unsecured at 10-K page:147). The asset-backed notes sit in unrestricted subsidiaries that hold fiber assets and customer contracts transferred from non-securitization subsidiaries, with no recourse to the company. After the July 2026 issue the asset-backed share rises from 16.8% to about 24.9% of principal before any repayments (calculated). Mechanism: assets move from the guarantor group to separate noteholders, so value available to the unsecured notes and the other secured creditors falls, and the asset sale offers show part of the proceeds must repay secured debt. Implication: unsecured holders are the most exposed to asset transfers. Legal capacity for transfers depends on indenture terms that are not supplied. - Liquidity is adequate but supplied by financing, not operations. Cash of 608.9 million and revolver availability of 838.1 million give 1,447.0 million; the Uniti Revolver provides 499.7 million and the Windstream Revolver 338.4 million after 136.6 million of letters of credit. Both revolvers mature 2027-12-30 and the Windstream Revolver commitment steps down after 2027-01-23. Implication: the revolver renewal in 2027 is the first liquidity event that depends on market conditions. - Equity-like claims sit ahead of common equity and can become cash claims. The preferred stock has a liquidation preference of 575.0 million and an 11% dividend, which is about 63.25 million a year at the face rate (calculated), and Elliott affiliates may require repurchase after the tenth anniversary. Mechanism: the repurchase may be settled in cash or stock. Implication: not a near-term cash issue, but it is a long-dated claim that competes with debt refinancing. - Data limits restrict the view. Covenant levels and compliance ratios, executed indentures and credit agreements, pro forma Adjusted EBITDA, the outcome of the July 2026 repayment offers and any report after 2026-07-30 are not supplied. A conflict on whether the 1.0 billion 8.625% notes are secured is logged and unresolved; the debt tables describe them as unsecured.

runs.text: - Scale and diversification of revenue. Three segments, no customer above 10% of revenue, and a network of about 240,000 fiber route miles (Documentary Fact, from the business handoff). Mechanism: reduces dependence on any one customer after the merger ended the dependence of Old Uniti on Windstream. Implication: lower single-customer default risk than before the merger. - Adequate near-term liquidity and no scheduled maturity before December 2027. Cash and revolver availability of 1,447.0 million, and no instrument maturing in the next twelve months other than term loan amortization (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation). Implication: low near-term refinancing and liquidity risk. - Demonstrated capital markets access. The company completed asset-backed notes in January and July 2026, 1.0 billion of unsecured notes in February 2026, and a secured refinancing in October 2025 that redeemed the 10.50% notes due 2028 (Documentary Fact). Implication: supports refinancing, though at high coupons. - Segment margins. Contribution margins of about 52% at Fiber Infrastructure, 50% at Uniti Solutions and 42% at Kinetic in Q2 2026 are stated by management (Management Language), before corporate costs. Implication: scope for operating leverage if revenue grows, not yet visible in cash flow. - No common dividends. The company states no intention to pay common dividends (Documentary Fact). Implication: cash is retained for the build and debt service. - Fiber customer growth. Kinetic fiber consumer broadband customers were 602.8 thousand at 2026-06-30 and management states record quarterly fiber net adds (Documentary Fact for the customer count; Management Language for the record claim). Implication: supports future recurring revenue, if build costs per premise are controlled, which is not shown.

- High leverage and thin cover. Total debt 7.16x and net debt 6.75x trailing Adjusted EBITDA, cash interest cover 1.94x (Documentary Fact and calculation from the financial base). Implication: little tolerance for earnings shortfalls or rate increases on the floating-rate term loan. - Negative free cash flow from the build. Operating cash flow of 339.4 million against capital expenditures of 799.2 million in H1 2026 (Documentary Fact). Implication: reliance on external funding. - GAAP losses. Net loss of 226.2 million in H1 2026 with interest expense, net of 383.9 million exceeding operating income of 143.1 million (Documentary Fact). Implication: earnings do not yet cover the interest burden on a GAAP basis. - Comparability and earnings quality. The perimeter changed on 2025-08-01, Adjusted EBITDA is a management measure, and Q1 2026 included IRU sales revenue of 85.5 million for the half that is not recurring service revenue (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on recurrence). Implication: run-rate earnings are harder to judge than reported trailing figures suggest. - Back-end loaded maturity wall and the shifting structure. Heavy 2031 to 2033 maturities, rising asset-backed debt in unrestricted subsidiaries, and a preferred stock claim with an Elliott repurchase right (Documentary Fact). Implication: refinancing risk is deferred rather than removed, and unsecured holders are more exposed to asset transfers. - Disclosure gaps and inconsistencies. No covenant levels, no executed documents, and two logged conflicts on ranking and the maturity table (Insufficient Information and Documentary Fact). Implication: the view cannot be tested against creditor protections.

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The Merger. On 2025-08-01 Windstream merged into the company, which survived as ultimate parent, and a merger subsidiary merged into Old Uniti, which survived as an indirect wholly owned subsidiary (Q2 10-Q page:9). Each Old Uniti share converted into 0.6029 shares of the company's common stock. Windstream's equityholders received about 90.1 million common shares, about 0.6 million preferred shares with a liquidation preference of 575.0, about 17.6 million warrants at a 0.01 dollar exercise price and 370.7 of cash, funded from Old Uniti's cash and revolver borrowings (page:10). The accounting is a reverse merger: Windstream was legal acquirer and Old Uniti was accounting acquirer (page:10). Total merger consideration was 2,376.6, made up of common stock 733.7, preferred stock 630.4, warrants 142.7, cash 370.7 and 499.1 attributed to the settlement of preexisting relationships (page:16). Those relationships were the Windstream Leases (an ILEC master lease and a CLEC master lease under which Old Uniti was Windstream's landlord), an asset purchase agreement and other leasing and supplier arrangements; they became intercompany and eliminated, and the leases were judged above market by 559.0 against an unfavourable asset purchase agreement of 60.0 (page:17-18). Status: complete; purchase price allocation finalised in Q2 2026 (page:18). Credit meaning: the Windstream lease payments that Old Uniti received as landlord ceased to be external revenue; creditors of the two former groups now rank in one structure.

Debt reorganisation. On 2025-08-04 Uniti Group LP, the borrower under Old Uniti's debt, was merged into Uniti Services LLC, formerly Windstream Services, LLC, the borrower under Windstream's debt. All debt became obligations of the same borrower, each subsidiary that guaranteed one group's debt guaranteed the other's, the Windstream revolver became pari passu with other first lien debt, and restrictive covenants that kept the groups apart were effectively eliminated (10-K page:56). Credit meaning: structural separation between the two creditor groups ended; the combined guarantor group supports all debt.

New debt issues, in date order, with status (all amounts in the financial base or the debt tables): - October 2025: 1.4 billion of 7.50% senior secured notes due 2033 and a new seven-year 1.0 billion term loan due 2032; proceeds redeemed in full the 10.50% secured notes due 2028 and added more than 100.0 of liquidity; 250.0 of secured fiber network revenue term notes with anticipated repayment in January 2031 were also issued (10-K page:56). Status: complete. - 2025: 600.0 of 8.625% senior unsecured notes issued 2025-06-24 under an indenture with Deutsche Bank Trust Company Americas as trustee (Q2 10-Q page:26). Status: complete. - 2026-01-30: Kinetic ABS 2026-1 notes of 960.1, secured by fiber network assets and residential customer contracts in Texas, Arkansas, Kentucky, Ohio and Georgia that were sold to the ABS obligors, which are unrestricted subsidiaries; no recourse to the company or other subsidiaries (Q2 10-Q page:26-29). The notes pay interest monthly, have no scheduled principal before the anticipated repayment date in February 2031, and carry rapid amortization if a debt service coverage ratio is not maintained (page:28, page:30). The indenture also provides for a variable funding note facility and up to 14.0 of liquidity funding notes, none outstanding (page:28-29). Status: complete. - 2026-02-04: 1.0 billion of 8.625% senior unsecured notes due 2032, expected to be exchanged for additional notes fungible with the existing 600.0; proceeds repaid the 500.0 Windstream Term Loan, revolver borrowings and funded general purposes including success-based capital expenditures (page:26). Gain on extinguishment of 1.2 (page:30). Status: complete. - 2026-07-15 (subsequent event): Kinetic ABS 2026-2 notes of 1,140.7, anticipated repayment June 2033, bought assets held by subsidiary guarantors of the company's senior debt that were contributed to Kinetic ABS subsidiaries; the company intends 500.0 of net proceeds to repay senior secured debt through a term loan prepayment offer and asset sale offers, and the rest for reinvestment including growth capital spending (page:52). Status: complete for the notes; the repayment offers were open at the filing date and their uptake is not supplied. - 2026-07-23 and 2026-07-30: term loan prepayment offer of up to 167.8, of which 19.8 was repaid on 2026-07-30, and asset sale offers for up to 332.2 of the 4.75% and 7.50% secured notes expiring 2026-08-20 unless extended (page:63; EX-99.1 2026-07-30 page:2). Status: outcome not supplied.

Credit meaning of the new issues: they extended the maturity profile and moved the funding of the Kinetic build to asset-level debt. The ABS structure ranks the noteholders first against the transferred assets, and the asset sale offers show that part of the proceeds is required to repay secured debt because the assets came from guarantor subsidiaries. How much cushion the restricted group retains depends on indenture terms that are not supplied.

fields.value: The registrant is Uniti Group Inc., the ultimate parent after the merger. On 2025-08-01 Windstream merged into the registrant and a merger subsidiary merged into Old Uniti, which survived as an indirect wholly owned subsidiary and ceased to be a REIT (Q2 10-Q page:9). The merger was accounted for as a reverse merger with Windstream as legal acquirer and Old Uniti as accounting acquirer, so periods before the merger show Old Uniti only (page:10-11). The Q2 10-Q states that Windstream is included from 2025-08-01 (page:19). fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt sits at several levels. Uniti Services LLC, CSL Capital, LLC and Uniti Group Finance 2019 Inc. are the borrowers under the Uniti Credit Agreement (page:23). Uniti Services, formerly Windstream Services, LLC, is the borrower under the Windstream Credit Agreement (page:24). The senior secured credit facilities are guaranteed by Uniti Group Inc. and Uniti Group LLC on a senior unsecured basis and by certain wholly owned subsidiaries of Uniti Services on a senior secured basis (page:25). Asset-backed notes are issued by bankruptcy-remote subsidiaries: Uniti Fiber ABS Issuer LLC and Uniti Fiber TRS Issuer LLC for the Fiber Infrastructure ABS Notes, and Kinetic ABS Issuer LLC for the Kinetic ABS Notes (page:22, page:50). Kinetic ABS Parent LLC and the Kinetic ABS obligors are unrestricted subsidiaries under the credit agreements and indentures (page:50). The Q2 10-Q gives a restricted versus unrestricted consolidating view of the balance sheet and statement of operations (page:50-51); the 10-K and earlier 10-Qs give the same view for their dates (10-K page:193-195; Q1 10-Q page:49; Q3 2025 10-Q page:66-67).

fields.value: The financial base is usable with limitations. Reported figures for Q1 2026, Q2 2026 and the first half of 2026 come from filed statements on the combined-company perimeter and tie to the releases. FY2025 holds the combined company only from 2025-08-01, so trailing and annual metrics are not like-for-like and are labelled that way. On the filed numbers, total debt principal of 10,680.6 million stood at 7.16x trailing-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of 1,492.2 million, and 6.75x after deducting 608.9 million of unrestricted cash. Trailing Adjusted EBITDA covered trailing cash interest paid of 768.6 million 1.94 times. Interest expense, net was 383.9 million in the first half of 2026 against GAAP operating income of 143.1 million, so the company reports a net loss of 226.2 million for the half. Operating cash flow of 339.4 million fell short of capital expenditures of 799.2 million, and the gap was funded by debt: 2,072.6 million of issuance against 930.0 million of repayments. Liquidity at 2026-06-30 was cash of 608.9 million plus 838.1 million of revolver availability. Four limits bind every metric: Adjusted EBITDA is a management measure defined to resemble debt agreement terms but not tested here; the trailing period includes July 2025 without Windstream; covenant levels are not printed; and quarter-end debt does not include the July 2026 asset-backed issue or the planned repayments.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Uniti Group Inc. is a Delaware holding company that survived the 2025-08-01 merger of Windstream and Old Uniti as the ultimate parent. Old Uniti was a REIT that owned and leased communications infrastructure, with Windstream as its anchor tenant; after the merger it ceased to be a REIT and the company does not qualify as one. The combined business has three segments. Kinetic sells consumer and small business broadband and voice in incumbent markets. Fiber Infrastructure sells enterprise, carrier and wholesale connectivity, including to hyperscalers, and holds the legacy fiber and leasing assets. Uniti Solutions sells managed network, security and collaboration services to enterprises. The credit story is the build-out of fiber to the home at Kinetic and of wholesale fiber, funded by debt. The creditor-relevant mechanics are these. First, the perimeter changed, so history before the merger is Old Uniti. Second, all pre-merger debt of Old Uniti and Windstream was merged into one borrower, Uniti Services LLC, with cross-guarantees and the removal of restrictive covenants that kept the groups apart. Third, since 2026-01-30 the company has financed Kinetic through asset-backed notes issued by bankruptcy-remote unrestricted subsidiaries that hold the fiber assets and customer contracts, which places those assets and their cash flows ahead of other creditors for those noteholders. Fourth, Elliott and its affiliates hold about 25.2% of the common stock and have rights tied to the preferred stock. Fifth, the company states that it does not intend to pay common dividends. No sponsor is named in the context. Behaviour toward creditors is read as neutral or mixed on documented actions: refinancing that extended the maturity profile and transparent disclosure of unrestricted subsidiary results on one side, and transfers of assets from guarantor subsidiaries into unrestricted asset-backed structures on the other. Legal capacity for those transfers depends on indenture terms that are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Merger. On 2025-08-01 Windstream merged into the company, which survived as ultimate parent, and a merger subsidiary merged into Old Uniti, which survived as an indirect wholly owned subsidiary (Q2 10-Q page:9). Each Old Uniti share converted into 0.6029 shares of the company's common stock. Windstream's equityholders received about 90.1 million common shares, about 0.6 million preferred shares with a liquidation preference of 575.0, about 17.6 million warrants at a 0.01 dollar exercise price and 370.7 of cash, funded from Old Uniti's cash and revolver borrowings (page:10). The accounting is a reverse merger: Windstream was legal acquirer and Old Uniti was accounting acquirer (page:10). Total merger consideration was 2,376.6, made up of common stock 733.7, preferred stock 630.4, warrants 142.7, cash 370.7 and 499.1 attributed to the settlement of preexisting relationships (page:16). Those relationships were the Windstream Leases (an ILEC master lease and a CLEC master lease under which Old Uniti was Windstream's landlord), an asset purchase agreement and other leasing and supplier arrangements; they became intercompany and eliminated, and the leases were judged above market by 559.0 against an unfavourable asset purchase agreement of 60.0 (page:17-18). Status: complete; purchase price allocation finalised in Q2 2026 (page:18). Credit meaning: the Windstream lease payments that Old Uniti received as landlord ceased to be external revenue; creditors of the two former groups now rank in one structure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt reorganisation. On 2025-08-04 Uniti Group LP, the borrower under Old Uniti's debt, was merged into Uniti Services LLC, formerly Windstream Services, LLC, the borrower under Windstream's debt. All debt became obligations of the same borrower, each subsidiary that guaranteed one group's debt guaranteed the other's, the Windstream revolver became pari passu with other first lien debt, and restrictive covenants that kept the groups apart were effectively eliminated (10-K page:56). Credit meaning: structural separation between the two creditor groups ended; the combined guarantor group supports all debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Uniti Group Inc. carries a weak fundamental credit profile with adequate near-term liquidity. The assessment is an Analyst Interpretation with Medium confidence. Financial risk dominates. At 2026-06-30 total debt principal of 10,680.6 million was 7.16x trailing Adjusted EBITDA and 6.75x net of unrestricted cash, and trailing Adjusted EBITDA covered trailing cash interest paid 1.94 times. Adjusted EBITDA is a company measure that excludes transaction costs and stock-based compensation, and the trailing window includes one pre-merger month. Cash generation does not support the investment programme: first-half 2026 operating cash flow of 339.4 million compared with capital expenditures of 799.2 million, so the build is financed with new debt, and the company reports a net loss in each of Q1 2026 and Q2 2026. Business risk is moderate. Uniti has three segments, no customer above 10% of revenue, a large fiber footprint, and a Kinetic fiber build that management intends to raise penetration and revenue per customer (management strategy), but the Fiber Infrastructure revenue base reset when Windstream's lease income ended on 2025-08-01, hyperscaler IRU revenue is lumpy, and the DSL base is declining. Liquidity is adequate for the next twelve months: 1,447.0 million of cash and revolver availability at 2026-06-30, no instrument maturing before the 2027-12-01 convertible notes and the 2027-12-30 revolver maturities, and 1,140.7 million of further asset-backed proceeds in July 2026 of which 500.0 million is planned for secured debt repayment. Creditor control and structure add risk: the share of debt in non-recourse asset-backed subsidiaries is rising, and covenant levels and executed documents are not supplied. The credit view is therefore that earnings must grow into the debt through the fiber build while market access stays open; the filings contain no evidence that either is secured.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leverage and cover are weak, and the apparent improvement is partly a perimeter effect. Total debt to trailing Adjusted EBITDA was 8.13x at FY2025, 7.75x at the trailing period to Q1 2026 and 7.16x at the trailing period to Q2 2026, but each earlier ratio uses a window with fewer Windstream months, so the improvement is partly a perimeter effect rather than a deleveraging. Cash interest cover was 1.78x, 2.34x and 1.94x on the same windows. Mechanism (Analyst Interpretation): higher-cost debt added in 2026 (8.625% unsecured notes and the asset-backed notes) is likely to raise cash interest faster than Adjusted EBITDA at the current build stage. Implication: leverage tolerance is low and a modest earnings shortfall would push trailing cash interest cover to about 1.55x (illustrative, calculated below).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Free cash flow is structurally negative while the build runs. Operating cash flow less capital expenditures was negative 459.8 million in H1 2026 and negative 437.6 million in FY2025. Adjusted EBITDA less capital expenditures for the trailing period was 151.4 million (calculated below), which does not cover trailing cash interest paid of 768.6 million. Mechanism: capital expenditures at Kinetic of 602.8 million in H1 2026 front-load cost before subscriber revenue. Implication: the company depends on debt issuance or asset monetisation to fund both the build and interest, and creditors depend on continued access to the asset-backed and bond markets.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Management's 2026 outlook implies interest absorbs most of the trend in earnings. The outlook for Adjusted EBITDA is 1,450 to 1,500 million, interest expense, net 805 million and a net loss of 480 to 530 million (management forward-looking statement). Against first-half interest expense, net of 383.9 million, the outlook implies about 421.1 million in the second half (calculated). Outlook Adjusted EBITDA covers outlook interest expense, net 1.80x to 1.86x (calculated). Implication: GAAP losses persist through 2026 on the company's own outlook.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Maturity profile is back-ended by instrument due dates but the printed table conflicts. By due date, 876.5 million falls due in 2027 and 2028 (the convertible notes and the 4.75% secured notes) and 7,405.1 million in 2031 to 2033. Within that, the 6.50% unsecured notes of 1,110.0 million fall due in 2029, and the 8.625% unsecured notes plus the 2025 Term Loan, 2,595.0 million together, fall due in 2032. The Q2 10-Q prints a maturity table that places 886.5 million in 2027 and 1,120.0 million in 2028, which differs from the due dates by one year for 2027 to 2030; the Q1 10-Q table agreed with the due dates. This corrects the financial base handoff, which said no maturity table was printed: one is printed at Q2 10-Q page:30. The credit view uses the due dates and flags the conflict. Implication: the wall by year is uncertain by one year for 2027 to 2030 until the company confirms the schedule; the total is not in question.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Structural priority is shifting toward asset-level debt. Of total principal, 6,964.1 million is secured (credit facility and secured notes 5,165.0 million plus asset-backed notes 1,799.1 million) and 3,716.5 million is senior unsecured, including the 2027 convertible notes (calculated; the convertible notes are described as senior unsecured at 10-K page:147). The asset-backed notes sit in unrestricted subsidiaries that hold fiber assets and customer contracts transferred from non-securitization subsidiaries, with no recourse to the company. After the July 2026 issue the asset-backed share rises from 16.8% to about 24.9% of principal before any repayments (calculated). Mechanism: assets move from the guarantor group to separate noteholders, so value available to the unsecured notes and the other secured creditors falls, and the asset sale offers show part of the proceeds must repay secured debt. Implication: unsecured holders are the most exposed to asset transfers. Legal capacity for transfers depends on indenture terms that are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity is adequate but supplied by financing, not operations. Cash of 608.9 million and revolver availability of 838.1 million give 1,447.0 million; the Uniti Revolver provides 499.7 million and the Windstream Revolver 338.4 million after 136.6 million of letters of credit. Both revolvers mature 2027-12-30 and the Windstream Revolver commitment steps down after 2027-01-23. Implication: the revolver renewal in 2027 is the first liquidity event that depends on market conditions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Equity-like claims sit ahead of common equity and can become cash claims. The preferred stock has a liquidation preference of 575.0 million and an 11% dividend, which is about 63.25 million a year at the face rate (calculated), and Elliott affiliates may require repurchase after the tenth anniversary. Mechanism: the repurchase may be settled in cash or stock. Implication: not a near-term cash issue, but it is a long-dated claim that competes with debt refinancing.

A conflict on whether the 1.0 billion 8.625% notes are secured is logged and unresolved; the debt tables describe them as unsecured.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Scale and diversification of revenue. Three segments, no customer above 10% of revenue, and a network of about 240,000 fiber route miles (Documentary Fact, from the business handoff). Mechanism: reduces dependence on any one customer after the merger ended the dependence of Old Uniti on Windstream. Implication: lower single-customer default risk than before the merger.

The source readiness handoff is the gate and is not itself graded. The review changes no figure in another handoff; where it disagrees it says so here, because an accepted handoff cannot be edited. fields.value: The evidence trace holds with one factual correction. Each material claim in the financial base, business context and credit synthesis was matched to a located source span or to a recomputation from located figures, and the three handoffs agree on every shared figure, period and perimeter label. The one claim that fails is in the financial base: it states that no debt maturity table is printed, while the second-quarter 10-Q prints one at page:30. The business context handoff found and logged the conflict between that table and the instrument due dates, and the credit synthesis carries the correction; the financial base itself cannot be edited, so the correction stands here. Four further claims are partly supported as wording, none changes a figure. The integrity verdict for the evaluated set is Restricted, not Committee Ready: the conclusions that matter most to a creditor, covenant headroom, the priority of asset-level debt against other creditors and the ranking of the 8.625% notes, rest on executed documents that are not in the sources. The cautious credit view with Medium confidence follows from the cited basis and is not overstated. The review is limited: the same session wrote and checked the handoffs, from the same extraction text, and locators are extraction chunks rather than printed pages.

fields.value: The strongest evidence against the cautious view is liquidity: cash of 608.9 and availability of 838.1 give 1,447.0 against no instrument maturity before 2027-12-01, and the company raised 1,140.7 more in July 2026. Segment contribution margins of about 52%, 50% and 42% suggest earnings power once the fiber build matures, and the 2026 outlook for Adjusted EBITDA of 1,450 to 1,500 compares with trailing 1,492.2, so the outlook range is close to the trailing figure. What would make that case win: capital expenditures falling after the build so that Adjusted EBITDA less capital expenditures covers interest, market access staying open for asset-backed and bond issuance, and the revolvers being extended before 2027-12-30. Downside chain with observable triggers: initiating condition, slower fiber penetration at Kinetic or fewer hyperscaler bookings; first operational break, Adjusted EBITDA below the low end of the outlook, which needs second-half Adjusted EBITDA of at least 651.3 (calculated); financial transmission, interest expense, net of 805 (outlook) then absorbs a larger share of earnings and cash interest cover falls below the trailing 1.94x; liquidity consequence, revolver drawings and letters of credit use the 838.1 of availability while capital expenditures continue; refinancing consequence, the 2027 maturities of the convertible notes and both revolvers meet a market that may be less open, while a failure of the debt service coverage test on the asset-backed notes would trigger rapid amortization of those notes (Q2 10-Q page:30). Observable triggers: quarterly Adjusted EBITDA against the 651.3 second-half requirement, the Windstream Revolver letter of credit balance, asset-backed debt service coverage disclosures, and the outcome of the asset sale offers.
